title: Shared-cache expansion: capacity is not payload compatibility
requiredVisibleLabel: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Resize cache with mixed readers; detect payload incompatibility masked by extra capacity.
sourceAcceptance: Scale cache capacity while keeping application access and payload compatibility intact.
parentAcceptance: Actual cache behavior, payload compatibility, and journey budgets remain valid; native resize limitations are disclosed.
preconditions: Standalone modern browser, no server, real cache, account, credentials or subscription.
One in-memory key holds Synthetic Ada / cart 3; both versions read and write it.
Fixed baseline capacity 4, demand 8, target 8 or 12; capacity units and latency are teaching values.
Original budget is frozen before resize and applies before, during and after the operation.
actions: Declare target capacity, writer payload, resize condition, coverage and original budget.
Request the synthetic resize and freeze settings.
Probe old/new reads and writes across three phases and inspect trace and gate.
Check a PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN interpretation independently of user impact.
Retain up to six attempts or explicitly reset all in-memory state.
trace: At most 18 observed operations and six immutable in-memory attempt histories.
assertions: More capacity improves modeled latency but never masks an incompatible old-reader payload.
Complete compatible overlap passes only if access and every original budget also pass.
Access gaps and earlier budget failures remain counted after capacity improves.
Missing old clients, empty samples and unverified capability cannot prove success.
Unsupported resize is rejected without claiming target capacity was applied.
Strict inputs, immutable authentic states and bounded history prevent invalid progress.
Actual DOM, keyboard, errors, reset, failure, unknown and CSP checks cover the exercise.
limits: Synthetic deterministic interleaving only, not real concurrent cache traffic or measured network latency.
No actual cache resize, mixed-client or payload interoperability certification.
B-S071 and D-S071 remain incomplete; native service/SKU/topology limitations require their own observation.
No production Node24, native/source-parent, five-nines or unattended browser lifecycle certification.
Published helper only; abandoned lifecycle prototype is unqualified.
File-origin Worker rejection precedes CSP; worker-src enforcement is not independently qualified.
Synthetic data only; no cloud, IaC, credentials, deployment, downloads, installs or spending.
One frozen S unit; tests, plumbing and refinement do not earn extra credit.
